name: The Local Church
overview: The local church is depicted in Scripture as a divinely established community where believers steadfastly devote themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, prayer, and the breaking of bread, demonstrating unity and mutual care (Acts 2:42). It is a body with many members, each having distinct roles, working together under the oversight of appointed leaders who shepherd the church purchased by Christ's own blood (Romans 12:4; Acts 20:28). The church serves as a visible testimony of God's manifold wisdom to spiritual powers and is to be regularly gathered for mutual encouragement, especially as the return of Christ approaches (Ephesians 3:10; Hebrews 10:25). Believers are called to submit to their leaders who watch over their souls with accountability before God, ensuring spiritual health and joy in ministry (Hebrews 13:17).
